sql: SELECT avail_season, avail_doy, value FROM climate WHERE index_id='oni' AND avail_season IN (1,2) AND avail_doy BETWEEN 40 AND 95 ORDER BY avail_season, avail_doy
SELECT ts_season, CAST(ts_doy/10 AS INT)*10 AS doy_bin, AVG(wtmp_c) avg_wtmp, COUNT(*) n FROM pier WHERE ts_season IN (1,2) AND ts_doy BETWEEN 50 AND 95 GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

SELECT fish_date_season, cls, CAST(fish_date_doy/10 AS INT)*10 AS doy_bin, SUM(yt)::FLOAT/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0) AS ypa, SUM(anglers) n_ang, COUNT(*) n_trips FROM trips WHERE fish_date_season IN (1,2) AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 50 AND 95 AND cls IN ('three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,2,1
SELECT report_date_doy, yt_local, yt_local_catch, yt_coronado, yt_all FROM fishdope WHERE report_date_season=2 AND report_date_doy BETWEEN 75 AND 91 ORDER BY report_date_doy

SELECT fish_date_doy, cls, SUM(yt) yt, SUM(anglers) ang, COUNT(*) n FROM trips WHERE fish_date_season=2 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 84 AND 91 AND cls IN ('three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT cls, boat, COUNT(*) n_days, MIN(fish_date_doy) min_d, MAX(fish_date_doy) max_d FROM schedule WHERE fish_date_season=2 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 91 AND 105 AND cls IN ('three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1, n_days DESC

# dope_solo notes — living doc. Read top section first (current plan), history below.

## CURRENT PLAN — as of Season 2, day 91 planning turn (21:00)
Status: $2000 / 10 PTO still fully intact, 0 bookings, 0 fish. Everyone on the
leaderboard is still at 0 — no disadvantage from waiting.

**Hard data confirms: the season-1 "spring spike" (doy 90-100) has NOT happened
in season 2.** Checked trips table directly, not just temp/ONI proxies:
- three_quarter/overnight/day_1_5 pooled ypa is **flat 0.0 in every 10-day bin
  from doy 50 through doy 90** (season 2), including a day-by-day check of
  doy 84-91 (10+ trips, 200+ angler-days, literally zero yellowtail landed on
  any of these classes). Season 1 at doy 90-100 was overnight ypa 2.8-3.9,
  three_quarter ~0.1-1.8 — night and day difference.
- Water stayed cold: Scripps Pier avg wtmp_c doy 90 bin = season2 14.9°C vs
  season1 16.0°C (~1.1°C colder), consistent with the whole doy50-90 season
  the gap held 1.0-1.6°C colder every bin, no narrowing trend.
- ONI: season2 avail_doy 71 = -1.29 (up slightly from -1.48 at doy40 — a small
  recovery, but still solidly strong-La-Niña-cold). Season1 at doy71 was
  +1.47 (El Niño). Huge structural difference between the two seasons.
- Fishdope: yt_local/yt_all were 0 through doy ~84, then a **small uptick
  doy85-91** (yt_local 1-3, yt_local_catch nonzero on 85/86/88/91, yt_coronado
  nonzero several days, yt_all hit 12 on doy91 — highest of the season so
  far). This is the first non-zero signal all season. NOT yet corroborated by
  actual trip counts (still 0 through doy91). Treat as an early watch flag,
  not a trigger — per persona, cross-check fishdope against counts before
  acting, and counts haven't turned yet.

**Decision for the nightly self, next ~2-3 weeks (doy 91-110ish):**
1. Still do NOT book HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT for yellowtail (dead classes,
   confirmed season 1, no reason to expect different in season 2).
2. Watch fishdope yt_local/yt_local_catch daily. If it keeps climbing for
   several more days AND the trips table (three_quarter is highest-frequency,
   check first) shows ypa clearly break above ~0.2-0.3, that's the trigger to
   test the water: book one cheap three_quarter ($150) first to confirm
   before committing to overnight/day_1_5. Boats currently scheduled doy
   91-105 for three_quarter: San Diego and Malihini run most often (good
   default pick_boat candidates), also Point Loma, Mission Belle. Overnight:
   Mustang, Voyager. Day_1_5: Constitution/Legend (doy92), Voyager (doy99).
3. If ypa confirms hot (>0.5+), escalate to overnight (season-1 spring
   economics: overnight was the best-sampled high-ypa vehicle, ~1.3-2.8 ypa
   at doy90-100) — only after real counts confirm, not on fishdope alone.
4. If fishdope stays flat/noisy and trips ypa stays ~0 through doy ~110-120,
   **write off the spring window entirely this year.** Cold La Niña water
   more than explains it. Don't force bets chasing the calendar. Roll the
   full $2000/10 PTO forward — this is actually a good position, since
   season-1 fall peak (doy ~260-310) was the single best window of the year
   and now we can go in with 100% of resources plus everything learned.
5. Because the cold start could also delay/shift the fall peak later than
   season-1's doy~280-300, **start watching fall signal earlier than before
   — by doy ~230 rather than doy 255** (temp trend, ONI, fishdope, trip
   counts). Don't pre-commit PTO by calendar date alone; commit only once
   signal actually confirms (remember: 14-day-ahead commitment lead time).
6. Competitive landscape unchanged: named strategies (B_SAT/B_PERSIST/B_TEMP)
   chase PM half-day (worthless for YT) and B_BIG plays Aug-Sep 1.5-day
   (Aug is historically trough; only helps them if the real peak is late).
   Expect little dilution on three_quarter/overnight/day_1_5 in Oct.

**Next planning turn checks:** re-pull trips ypa for three_quarter (daily,
doy 91-current) — this is the fastest-confirming class since it runs most
often. Re-pull ONI (next monthly print ~doy 100). Re-check fishdope yt_local
trend. If a spring bite materialized, note which boats scored best. If not,
just confirm still-flat and move on — don't over-spend query budget re-
deriving the same season-1 baseline numbers (already well documented below).

---

## Season-1 baseline reference (for comparison only — do not assume season 2 repeats this calendar)
- Half-day/twilight classes are ~dead for YT all year (ypa ~0.00-0.01) in
  every window checked. Never book them.
- Season 1 windows: doy90-100 spike (ypa~0.86 pooled, overnight 1.8-2.8),
  dip 100-130, moderate 130-180, TROUGH 180-260 (worst water, most fleet
  volume), FALL PEAK 260-310 (best of year, day_1_5 ypa 2.19 n=73, overnight
  0.60 n=71 in 270-310; day_1_5 was even higher in spring but thin sample).
- Season 1 class economics in good windows: day_1_5 > overnight > three_quarter
  per-trip, but day_1_5 samples were thin in spring (trust overnight there);
  fall peak day_1_5 sample is large and convincing.
- Fishdope vs pooled fleet ypa correlation: same-day ~+0.28, next-day ~+0.18
  (weak-ish but real). Weight yt_local/yt_coronado (SD-reachable) over yt_all
  (includes Catalina/Channel Islands we can't fish).
- Budget/PTO pacing (original plan, now superseded by "roll forward" logic
  above if spring is a bust): ~$1400-1600 + 5-6 PTO reserved for fall peak,
  ~$400-600 + a few PTO for spring window. Friday departures for
  overnight/day_1_5 save PTO (0 PTO if back Sun/Mon-holiday).

## Season 2 cold-water confirmation timeline
- Day 1: ONI ~-1.6 vs season1 ~+1.3-1.5 at same point — flagged La Niña risk.
- Day 32: still -1.48 (doy40), pier temp ~1.0-1.4°C colder, no warming trend.
- Day 60: no new ONI print yet, pier gap holding steady 1.0-1.4°C colder.
- Day 91 (this turn): ONI recovered slightly to -1.29 (doy71) but still cold;
  pier gap still ~1.1-1.6°C colder through doy90; **trips table now directly
  confirms zero yellowtail on three_quarter/overnight/day_1_5 through doy91**,
  vs season1's real spring spike at this point. Fishdope shows first faint
  uptick doy85-91 — watch, don't act yet.

## Open items
- Boat-level variance within a class not yet analyzed (which specific boat
  outfishes peers) — do this once a real signal window opens and there's
  count history to compare boats on.
- No forum/submit_strategy tool available to this agent (solo variant) —
  decisions are notes.md + nightly briefing judgment only.
